candidates.explanation: I couldn't see this method's source, so this is inferred and the line numbers are estimates. AuthService.update calls MailService.confirmNewEmail, which the snippets don't show. It most likely builds the link from the sign-up route '/confirm-email', copied from userSignUp. The correct route is '/confirm-new-email'. The email-change link therefore opens the sign-up activation page. That page treats the hash as a sign-up confirmation, so the email change never completes. The method may also reuse the 'activation.hbs' template instead of 'confirm-new-email.hbs', or the sign-up i18n keys.

This builds the email-change hash as a JWT with confirmEmailUserId and newEmail, signed with the same confirmEmailSecret and expiry as the sign-up hash. It then passes the hash to mailService.confirmNewEmail. If the mail call or the token payload is wrong, the link will not complete the email change. This is less likely than the mail service.

fix.description: In MailService.confirmNewEmail, build the URL with frontendDomain + '/confirm-new-email' instead of '/confirm-email'. Use the 'confirm-new-email.hbs' template and the confirm-new-email i18n keys. Keep setting the 'hash' search param. The frontend and the backend endpoint can then process the new-email token.
